prompt: For each parent category, what is the average net revenue of a single-unit order line, and of a multi-unit line? Use the sales table. A single-unit line has units of exactly 1, and a multi-unit line has units of 2 or more; a line with missing units is neither. Return three columns, in this order: parent_category, avg_single_line_eur, the average net_revenue_eur over the category's single-unit lines, and avg_multi_line_eur, the average net_revenue_eur over its multi-unit lines. Lines with a missing net_revenue_eur are left out of the averages, and when a category has no such lines, that average is missing. Return one row per parent_category. Do not round. Any row order is fine.
hints: Next, write the two average columns, each averaging only one kind of line.

Put a CASE inside AVG that gives net_revenue_eur for the right kind of line, and leave out ELSE: a 0 for every other line would be averaged in, but a missing value is skipped. Two units already counts as multi-unit.
why_this_works: Without ELSE, the CASE gives a missing value for the other kind of line, and AVG skips missing values, so each average divides by its own lines only.
